references.text: Moses went out from Pharaoh and prayed to the Lord, following the same pattern seen here where Moses leaves Pharaoh to pray.
Moses prays to the Lord on behalf of Pharaoh to remove the plague of frogs, a similar intercessory pattern.
Moses went out from Pharaoh and stretched out his hands toward the Lord, the same action of leaving Pharaoh to pray to God.
Moses and Aaron were brought back to Pharaoh, providing context for the conversation that leads to Moses' intercession.
Isaac prayed earnestly to the Lord (וַיֶּעְתַּר), using the same Hebrew verb for earnest prayer.
God allowed Himself to be entreated (וַיֵּעָתֶר), using the same root verb that shows God's response to earnest prayer.
Another episode where Moses had to leave Pharaoh to pray for intervention against a plague, highlighting the pattern in how he carried out his calling.
A parallel in Numbers 4 where Moses' prayer immediately stops a judgment (fire), reflecting the dynamic seen in the departure.
